summary: John M. Koller is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena and Charles Alexander Moore. He served as a professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, attested in 1988 and 1999.

John M. Rosenfield was a scholar of art history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Benjamin Rowland and served as Harvard's Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of East Asian Art from 1965 to 1991.

John Marshall was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at King's College, Cambridge, and under Arthur Evans. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1902 to 1931.

John Muir was an Indologist who studied at the University of Glasgow, East India Company College, and University of Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853) and was principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1844.
John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Namkhai Norbu.

John Nemec is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Rochester, UC Santa Barbara, Oxford, and Penn, under Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher. In 2020 he was attested as Associate Professor at the University of Virginia.

John Newman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida (attested 1996–2000).

John Okell was a linguist who studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, and under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. He served as a research associate at SOAS University of London from 1959 to 1999.

John P. Keenan is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held posts at Nanzan University (1983–1986) and Middlebury College (attested 1989 and 2006).

John Peile was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge, and under Theodor Benfey. He served as Fellow and Tutor at Christ's College (~1860–1910) and Reader of Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1884–1891).
John Pickford was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He held a post as Professor at the University of Madras.

John Powers is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his doctorate from the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. His appointments include the Australian National University (1995) and Deakin University (2016–2022).

John R. B. Campbell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, while also studying under several traditional and academic teachers.

John R. McRae was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He held teaching posts at Cornell (~1988–1995), Indiana University (~1996–2005), and Komazawa University (~2006–2008).
John Raines was a religious studies scholar who studied at Carleton College and Union Theological Seminary. He held an academic post at Temple University from ~1965 to 2011.
John Riley Perks is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teachers Dilgo Khyentse and the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

John Ross Carter was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed doctoral work at Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith. He served as a professor at Colgate University's Chapel House from ~1972 to 2006.

John S. Strong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds. He served as a professor of religious studies at Bates College from ~1978 to 2017.

John Shakespear was an Indologist and linguist who studied under John Richardson. He held professorships of oriental languages at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805–1809) and Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).
John Shore was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. Succeeding William Jones, he served as President of The Asiatic Society.
